description: Curated control rows for data/control-points.json (PRD-SETPOINT-SIM B1). HAND-WRITTEN and reviewed. tools/build-control-registry.mjs reads it. A setpoint here names the engine parameter that holds it; its value, source and evidence class come from the engine registry, never from this file. `adjustable` exists only with a written basis.

convSetpoints.label: Chilled water supply setpoint
convSetpoints.control: leaving chilled water temperature held by the chiller capacity control; the engine derives it from the CRAH supply air less the coil approach
convSetpoints.adjustableNote: derived: it moves when its drivers move (rack-inlet target, coil approach), never on its own

pv.what: leaving chilled-water temperature at the evaporator outlet nozzle

mv.what: compressor capacity of this chiller: drive speed first, inlet guide vanes at low load

out.what: compressor drive speed of a running chiller

loop.tuningNote: not modelled: the chiller's own unit controller; no source states its gain or time constant
loop.basis: vendor unit-controller practice (ASSUMED structure; no vendor manual in this repo): the unit panel modulates capacity to hold leaving chilled water; direct acting (temperature rises, capacity rises)

convSetpoints.label: CRAH supply air setpoint
convSetpoints.control: supply air temperature held by the CRAH chilled-water valve; the engine sets it equal to the rack-inlet target (no bypass or recirculation modelled)

pv.what: supply-air temperature leaving the unit to the cold aisle

mv.what: two-way chilled-water valve of this unit (coil flow)

out.what: chilled-water valve opening (coil flow / design flow) of a running CRAH

loop.tuningNote: not modelled: the CRAH's own unit controller; no source states its gain or time constant
loop.basis: ASHRAE Guideline 36-2021 (air-handler supply-air temperature control by the cooling-coil valve); direct acting for a cooling coil (temperature rises, valve opens)

convSetpoints.label: Rack inlet temperature target
convSetpoints.control: the cold-aisle condition the air system is designed and reset to

adjustable.basis: ASHRAE TC9.9 Thermal Guidelines (5th ed.), class A1 recommended envelope 18–27 °C
adjustable.stepBasis: 0.1 K, the resolution the engine parameter is stated in (25.4 °C)

convSetpoints.whatIfNote: Steady state of the engine: the rack inlet target resets the CRAH supply air and the CHW supply that follow it. PUE is a model input (site.pue) in this engine, so no setpoint moves it. Dynamics (how fast the plant gets there) are not modelled. TIC-SAT output (P10): the CRAH valve opening is coil flow / design flow at the duty count; the engine does not re-rate the coil for a colder supply air, so the valve does not move with this setpoint here: whether a CRAH can hold a lower setpoint at 99.5 % is not modelled.

pv.what: rack inlet temperature in the contained cold aisle

mv.what: the TIC-SAT setpoint of every running CRAH (contained aisle, no mixing modelled: slave setpoint = master setpoint)

loop.tuningNote: not modelled: a reset sets the slave setpoint; the engine solves the steady state
loop.notDrawn: no P&ID on the data hall page: the rack-inlet target resets TIC-SAT, drawn inside each CRAH
loop.basis: ASHRAE TC9.9 Thermal Guidelines (rack inlet is the controlled condition) and ASHRAE Guideline 36-2021 supply-air temperature reset

convSetpoints.label: Condenser water supply setpoint
convSetpoints.control: tower leaving water temperature held by the tower fan speed
convSetpoints.adjustableNote: no floor is declared yet: the lowest reachable value is the design wet-bulb plus the tower approach, and the chiller's minimum lift; adjustable when both are in the engine

pv.what: condenser water supply temperature from the tower basins

mv.what: fan speed of every running tower cell

out.what: fan speed of the running tower cells

loop.tuningNote: not modelled: no source states this loop's gain or time constant; the engine solves the steady state
loop.basis: ASHRAE Guideline 36-2021 (high-performance sequences of operation for HVAC systems): tower fans modulate to hold the condenser water supply setpoint; direct acting (temperature rises, fan speed rises)

convSetpoints.label: Secondary loop differential pressure setpoint
convSetpoints.control: remote differential pressure held by the secondary pump speed

adjustable.basis: the chiller-plant page's DP setpoint range (60–140 kPa), the range the engine parameter states as its source

whatIf.label: Secondary pump input power, running fleet

convSetpoints.whatIfNote: Steady state of the engine: the pump speed its curve needs to hold this differential pressure, and the input power at that operating head (engine 2.10.0). The loop flow is set by the load, not by this setpoint, so the power moves little. PUE is a model input and does not move. Dynamics are not modelled.

pv.what: differential pressure across the most remote CRAH bank

mv.what: speed of every running secondary pump (VSD)

out.what: mean speed of the running secondary pumps

loop.tuningNote: not modelled: no source states this loop's gain or time constant; the engine solves the steady state
loop.basis: ASHRAE Guideline 36-2021 (high-performance sequences of operation for HVAC systems): variable-speed distribution pumps held at a remote differential-pressure setpoint; reverse acting (DP falls, speed rises)

convSetpoints.pvNote: PDT-01 on CH-M-101 (engine steady state, which holds this setpoint). Not the KPI 'Header DP' (chiller-plant.CHW.header_dp): that is the mean of the primary loops' authored DPS1/DPS2, a different quantity

dcaiValueEvidence.note: A DC AI point record that TYPES its reference value (sp.value in js/datahall-ai/points.js) has no source for that number of its own: it is ASSUMED unless listed here with the reason.

sld-mv-sub/bus_kv.why: 20 kV is the nominal system voltage (IEC 60038 / SPLN 1)

sld-rmu/bus_kv.why: 20 kV is the nominal system voltage (IEC 60038 / SPLN 1)

sld-mv-sub/frequency.why: 50 Hz is the nominal frequency of the PLN grid (Grid Code Jawa-Madura-Bali)

rack-busbar/vdc.why: 48 VDC is the shelf output voltage of the rack power design

chem/ph.why: the page's own control window 8.2–8.8; 8.5 is its centre

dcaiPlaneController.note: Which DC AI point class HOLDS each engine design plane (its controller acts on it). On that class the plane is a setpoint; on every other class that reads the same plane it is a reference, with heldBy naming the controller. A plane with no controller among the DC AI point classes is a reference everywhere.

p07_tcs_supply_c.why: the CDU holds TCS supply with its HX control valve

p02_dry_cooler_leaving_c.why: the dry cooler holds its leaving water with fan speed

p12_chw_supply_c.why: the chiller holds leaving chilled water with its capacity control

p09_air_supply_c.why: the CRAH holds supply air with its chilled-water valve

dcaiTypedSetpoints.note: DC AI point records whose typed value IS a control setpoint (a controller holds it); every other typed value is a reference (nameplate, nominal, design value).
dcaiTypedSetpoints.crah/supply_rh: humidity setpoint of the CRAH humidifier / dehumidification control
dcaiTypedSetpoints.chem/ph: pH control point of the dosing controller
dcaiTypedSetpoints.chem/conductivity: conductivity setpoint of the blowdown controller
dcaiTypedSetpoints.chem/orp: ORP control point of the biocide dosing
dcaiTypedSetpoints.chem/inhibitor_ppm: inhibitor residual target of the dosing controller
dcaiTypedSetpoints.stp/do_mgl: dissolved-oxygen control of the aeration blowers
dcaiTypedSetpoints.ahu/supply_c: supply-air temperature control of the MMR air-handling unit
dcaiTypedSetpoints.room/temp_c: room thermostat of the support-room HVAC
dcaiTypedSetpoints.site-genset-yard/jacket_c: keep-warm thermostat of the jacket-water heater

dcaiAdjustable.note: PRD-SETPOINT-SIM §C P6. DC AI setpoints an operator can move, keyed by point id; the what-if is DCAI_CALC.compute on a copy of the model with param changed.

adjustable.basis: upper 45 °C: ASHRAE TC9.9 liquid cooling class W45 (facility water ≤ 45 °C); lower 30 °C: dew-point margin, ASSUMED

whatIf.label: Ambient where liquid free cooling ends
Free-cooling hours a year (shaped bins, ASSUMED)

cdu/tcs_supply_c.whatIfNote: Steady state of the DC AI engine at the design point (design ambient 34 °C, shaped weather bins ASSUMED, not a TMY file); dynamics not modelled; nothing is saved.

adjustable.basis: ASHRAE TC9.9 Thermal Guidelines (5th ed.), class A1 recommended inlet 18–27 °C; contained aisle, rack inlet = supply air

crah/air_supply_c.whatIfNote: Steady state of the DC AI engine at the design point (design ambient 34 °C, shaped weather bins ASSUMED, not a TMY file); dynamics not modelled; nothing is saved.

convPageSetpoints.label: Jockey pump start (header pressure falls to)
convPageSetpoints.control: the jockey pump controller PC-JP1 (its pressure switch on its own sensing line from the discharge) starts the jockey pump
convPageSetpoints.basis: NFPA 20 (2022) Annex A.14.2.6 practice: jockey stop = churn + minimum static; jockey start >= 0.7 bar (10 psi) below its stop; the main pump starts 0.35 bar (5 psi) below the jockey start; each further pump >= 0.7 bar (10 psi) lower. The values are this page's design (ASSUMED: no site hydraulic calculation in this repository); law T3 checks the spacing.
convPageSetpoints.pvNote: the header pressure is the page's simulated state (PT on the header), not yet a point of the limits registry

pv.what: discharge pressure through the controller's own sensing line, tapped between the pump's discharge check valve and its discharge isolation valve

mv.what: jockey pump JP-01: start at the cut-in, stop at the cut-out

loop.tuningNote: on-off with a differential (cut-in to cut-out); no gain or time constant
loop.basis: NFPA 20 (2022): each fire-pump and jockey-pump controller has its own pressure-sensing line, connected between the pump's discharge check valve and its discharge isolation valve, and starts its pump when the pressure falls to its cut-in; the staggered cut-ins (A.14.2.6 practice) are the registry numbers. On-off: no gain or time constant applies.

convPageSetpoints.label: Jockey pump stop (header pressure rises to)
convPageSetpoints.control: the jockey pump controller stops the jockey pump
convPageSetpoints.basis: NFPA 20 (2022) Annex A.14.2.6 practice: jockey stop = churn + minimum static; jockey start >= 0.7 bar (10 psi) below its stop; the main pump starts 0.35 bar (5 psi) below the jockey start; each further pump >= 0.7 bar (10 psi) lower. The values are this page's design (ASSUMED: no site hydraulic calculation in this repository); law T3 checks the spacing.
convPageSetpoints.pvNote: the header pressure is the page's simulated state (PT on the header), not yet a point of the limits registry

convPageSetpoints.label: Main fire pump 1 start
convPageSetpoints.control: the fire pump 1 controller (NFPA 20 listed) starts on falling header pressure
convPageSetpoints.basis: NFPA 20 (2022) Annex A.14.2.6 practice: jockey stop = churn + minimum static; jockey start >= 0.7 bar (10 psi) below its stop; the main pump starts 0.35 bar (5 psi) below the jockey start; each further pump >= 0.7 bar (10 psi) lower. The values are this page's design (ASSUMED: no site hydraulic calculation in this repository); law T3 checks the spacing.
convPageSetpoints.pvNote: the header pressure is the page's simulated state (PT on the header), not yet a point of the limits registry

pv.what: discharge pressure through the controller's own sensing line, tapped between the pump's discharge check valve and its discharge isolation valve

mv.what: main fire pump FP-01 (electric): start at the cut-in; stop by hand (the page models no automatic stop)

loop.tuningNote: start only; no gain or time constant
loop.basis: NFPA 20 (2022): each fire-pump and jockey-pump controller has its own pressure-sensing line, connected between the pump's discharge check valve and its discharge isolation valve, and starts its pump when the pressure falls to its cut-in; the staggered cut-ins (A.14.2.6 practice) are the registry numbers. On-off: no gain or time constant applies.

convPageSetpoints.label: Main fire pump 2 start
convPageSetpoints.control: the fire pump 2 controller starts on falling header pressure, staggered below pump 1
convPageSetpoints.basis: NFPA 20 (2022) Annex A.14.2.6 practice: jockey stop = churn + minimum static; jockey start >= 0.7 bar (10 psi) below its stop; the main pump starts 0.35 bar (5 psi) below the jockey start; each further pump >= 0.7 bar (10 psi) lower. The values are this page's design (ASSUMED: no site hydraulic calculation in this repository); law T3 checks the spacing.
convPageSetpoints.pvNote: the header pressure is the page's simulated state (PT on the header), not yet a point of the limits registry

pv.what: discharge pressure through the controller's own sensing line, tapped between the pump's discharge check valve and its discharge isolation valve

mv.what: main fire pump FP-02 (diesel): start at the cut-in; stop by hand (the page models no automatic stop)

loop.tuningNote: start only; no gain or time constant
loop.basis: NFPA 20 (2022): each fire-pump and jockey-pump controller has its own pressure-sensing line, connected between the pump's discharge check valve and its discharge isolation valve, and starts its pump when the pressure falls to its cut-in; the staggered cut-ins (A.14.2.6 practice) are the registry numbers. On-off: no gain or time constant applies.

convPageSetpoints.label: Header low-pressure alarm
convPageSetpoints.basis: below both pump starts, so it only sounds when the pumps cannot hold the header; value is this page's design (ASSUMED)
convPageSetpoints.pvNote: the header pressure is the page's simulated state (PT on the header), not yet a point of the limits registry

convPageSetpoints.label: Day-tank fill start (running set)
convPageSetpoints.control: the day-tank level controller opens the fill valve and calls transfer pump P-101
convPageSetpoints.basis: NFPA 110 (2022) §7.9.1 requires a day tank sized and refilled to keep the set running; start and stop levels are this page's design (ASSUMED, no source states them)

pv.what: day-tank level, from the tank's own level transmitter

mv.what: day-tank fill valve XV-nn: opens at the fill start (and calls the transfer pump), closes at the fill stop

loop.tuningNote: on-off with a differential (fill start to fill stop); no gain or time constant
loop.basis: Day-tank practice in the NFPA 110 / NFPA 30 context: a level controller on each day tank opens its fill valve on low level and closes it on high level; the start / stop levels are the registry numbers (ASSUMED page design). nn = the genset set (DT-GEN-A1 -> LIC-A1 -> XV-A1). On-off: no gain or time constant applies.

convPageSetpoints.label: Day-tank fill stop
convPageSetpoints.control: the day-tank level controller closes the fill valve (high level)
convPageSetpoints.basis: leaves 10 % headspace below the overflow; this page's design (ASSUMED)

convPageSetpoints.label: Day-tank level kept while fill is available
convPageSetpoints.basis: the fill answers within a few scans, so a running set's tank never falls below this; 45 % of 4 h = 1.8 h at rated burn (checked by tools/test-conv-fuel-truth.mjs)

convPageSetpoints.label: Day-tank low-low alarm
convPageSetpoints.basis: this page's design (ASSUMED); the point band lo_alarm 25 % agrees

convPageSetpoints.label: TCS supply (TCV-01 holds TT-01)
convPageSetpoints.control: TCV-01, the CDU three-way valve, holds the secondary supply TT-01 (direct acting PI in the unit controller)
convPageSetpoints.basis: per CDU type, the supply this page's model runs at; ASHRAE TC9.9 liquid-cooling W classes cap it (W32 / W40); the floor is room dew point + 3 K (18 °C, the point's low warning)

pv.what: TCS secondary supply temperature, TT-01 on the supply header to the rack

mv.what: three-way facility-water valve TCV-01 on the liquid-to-liquid types; on the air-cooled L2A type (no facility water) the air-coil fan speed

loop.tuningNote: no source for Kp / Ti; the page shows steady states only (dynamics not modelled)
loop.basis: CDU unit control as vendors describe it: the secondary supply transmitter feeds the unit controller, which positions the facility-water valve (or, liquid-to-air, the coil fans) to hold the supply. Direct acting: supply above the setpoint opens the valve (more facility water through E-01).

convPageSetpoints.label: TCS loop dP (P-01 VFD holds PDT-02)
convPageSetpoints.control: PDIC-02 holds the secondary loop differential pressure PDT-02 with the duty pump's VFD (P-01A, or P-01B after an N+1 changeover)
convPageSetpoints.basis: per CDU type, the loop dP this page's model runs at (page design; no source states these numbers). Variable-speed CDU pumps on a constant loop differential pressure is common CDU practice; the cold-plate manifold needs a minimum dP for its flow, and the point's band (0.5 to 3.0 bar) brackets every type.

mv.what: the duty pump's variable-frequency drive (P-01A, or P-01B after an N+1 changeover); the speed itself is not modelled on this page

loop.tuningNote: no source for Kp / Ti; the page shows steady states only (dynamics not modelled)
loop.basis: Constant-dP pumping: the loop dP transmitter feeds the controller, which trims the duty pump speed. Reverse acting: dP below the setpoint raises the speed. The fault scenarios (filter clog, low flow, pump trip) move the PV off its setpoint because the page models the fault, not the controller's recovery.

convPageSetpoints.label: TCS supply floor (room dew point + 3 K)
convPageSetpoints.basis: hold the secondary supply at least 3 K above the room dew point (ASHRAE TC9.9 liquid cooling guidance); it is the TT-01 point's low warning, and the builder refuses a different number

convPageSetpoints.label: Booster discharge pressure setpoint (PT-301)
convPageSetpoints.control: the booster set controller PIC-301 holds the discharge pressure at PT-301 with the duty pump's speed (lead/lag pair P-301A/B)
convPageSetpoints.basis: A constant-pressure booster set (variable-speed duty pump, lead/lag standby) holds its discharge at a setpoint, as booster-set practice for building water service does (EN 806-2 / ASPE pressure-booster design). The value is this page's design: the drawing declared it for PT-301 before the registry (water-system.html pt301Bar); no site hydraulic calculation is in this repository, so it is ASSUMED.
convPageSetpoints.pvNote: the discharge pressure is the page's simulated state at PT-301 (steady state: the controller holds it at its setpoint), not yet a point of the limits registry

pv.what: booster discharge pressure, transmitter PT-301 on the header after the pump pair

mv.what: duty booster pump P-301A speed (VSD); the speed itself is not modelled on this page

loop.tuningNote: no source for Kp / Ti; the page shows steady states only (dynamics not modelled)
loop.basis: Pressure-booster practice: the transmitter on the common discharge feeds the set controller, which trims the duty pump speed to hold the setpoint and calls the lag pump when the duty pump is at full speed. Reverse acting: pressure below the setpoint raises the speed.

dcaiLoops.note: PRD-SETPOINT-SIM P10 part 2: the loop that holds a DC AI setpoint and the engine key of its output (A8a equal-percentage valve stroke). Tags as drawn; nn = the unit number (CDU-01: TT-013 -> TIC-011 -> TV-011).

cdu/tcs_supply_c.tuningNote: tuning not modelled (no source for Kp / Ti)
cdu/tcs_supply_c.basis: TCS supply above SP opens the facility-water valve (more heat to the HX); stroke = the engine's equal-percentage valve at the duty per CDU (js/dcai-engine.js valveStroke, A8a)

crah/air_supply_c.tuningNote: tuning not modelled (no source for Kp / Ti)
crah/air_supply_c.notDrawn: the fan-wall unit sheet (FW-nn) draws TT-nn2 and TV-nn with their signals, not the controller
crah/air_supply_c.basis: supply air above SP opens the chilled-water valve (more coil duty); stroke = the engine's equal-percentage valve at the duty per fan-wall unit (js/dcai-engine.js valveStroke, A8a)
